headline: Showers today give way to a stormy week for western Washington, with a stronger storm Tuesday into Wednesday and another Wednesday night into Thursday bringing widespread rain, gusty winds, mountain snow and a growing coastal flood threat, including higher tides along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday on.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A low-pressure system parked off the coast keeps sending showers ashore through Sunday afternoon, so Sequim, Port Angeles and the Puget Sound lowlands can expect on-and-off showers, with the most active ones along the coast, where a few could turn briefly stormy this afternoon. Highs are near normal for late November, in the mid 40s to near 50. Snow levels drop to about 2,000–3,000 feet late tonight, and a Winter Weather Advisory runs from 6 PM Sunday to 4 PM Monday for the Olympics, where Hurricane Ridge could see 5 to 10 inches of snow.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Monday brings a wave of steadier precipitation, mostly focused on the Olympics and Cascades, with showers over the interior lowlands and snow levels rising to about 4,000 feet by afternoon. Another front arrives Tuesday, and a stronger one moves over western Washington Tuesday into Wednesday as the offshore low deepens, bringing widespread lowland rain, mountain snow with Cascade snow levels around 3,000–3,500 feet, and locally breezy winds, strongest along the coast.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: More strong storms follow Wednesday into Thursday (Thanksgiving) with another round of widespread rain, breezy winds and mountain snow, with rain heaviest Wednesday night into Thursday, especially over the Olympics. No widespread river flooding is expected, but the Skokomish River will likely reach minor flood stage around midweek and stay there through the weekend; a Hydrologic Outlook has been issued. Winds turn more southerly to southwesterly on Thanksgiving Day, and the discussion says little about Friday and Saturday on land beyond a brief lull in the wind Friday morning.

coast: A Coastal Flood Advisory runs until 3 PM Sunday for the Grays Harbor County and northern Washington coasts. High tides plus the coming storms raise the coastal flood threat, especially along the Pacific coast during Tuesday's high surf, and confidence is increasing that moderate to major flooding could occur along parts of the Grays Harbor County coast with Wednesday's tides, made worse by high surf. Tides rise more significantly along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines (including the Sequim and Port Angeles shore) from Tuesday onward, and impacts there will be watched closely. On the water, southeast winds of 23–35 mph (20–30 knots) continue today over the coastal waters and the east Strait, with a slight chance of thunderstorms over the coastal waters this afternoon and evening; a Small Craft Advisory covers the east entrance of the Strait until 10 PM Sunday, followed there by a Gale Warning from 10 PM Sunday to 10 PM Monday, while the central and west Strait, Admiralty Inlet and the San Juans have a Small Craft Advisory over the same hours, and the Grays Harbor Bar has one until 10 PM Monday as seas build to 9–12 feet. Monday evening through late Tuesday looks worst offshore, with widespread gale-force gusts and a better than 60% chance of storm-force gusts (about 55 mph or more) in the outer coastal waters, where a Storm Warning runs from 7 AM Monday to 10 AM Tuesday. Another round of strong gales comes Wednesday into Thursday (50% chance of storm-force gusts), with interior waters seeing more wind on Thanksgiving as winds turn south-southwest; after a brief break Friday morning it stays breezy offshore into the weekend. Seas build to 18–22 feet Tuesday, ease to 16–20 feet Wednesday and Thursday, and drop to 10–12 feet Friday into the weekend.
watch_for: Coastal flooding: moderate to major flooding possible on the Grays Harbor County coast with Wednesday's high tides, and rising tides along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday onward.
Skokomish River likely in minor flood from midweek through the weekend.
Gales on the Strait Sunday night into Monday, and the strength of the Tuesday and Wednesday–Thursday storms.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in showers today and an active, stormy pattern through the week, with growing confidence in coastal flooding along the Grays Harbor County coast Wednesday, while impacts along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines later in the week remain uncertain and will be watched closely.
